scope.description: One-off Canadian company research prompted by a real beta query for modular containerized naval solutions. The batch deliberately separates container fabrication, deployable mission-container integration, military shelter integration, naval-platform integration, and a comparable Royal Canadian Navy modular project.

source.title: CTS Containers Services and Capabilities
source.locator: Services overview and ISO Shipping Container Modifications sections
source.summary: CTS describes custom container design and manufacturing, structural and interior modification, electrical and HVAC fit-outs, ISO and CSC testing, prototype work, and DNV 2.7-1 certification support from its Dartmouth facility.

leads.evidenceLocator: Official about, services, modification, testing, certification, and public contact sections
followUpQuestions: Is there an approved public source that identifies a defence or Royal Canadian Navy project delivered by CTS?
Which current certifications and maximum container sizes should be displayed publicly?
leads.roleSpecificEvidence: CTS publicly documents in-house design, custom ISO and offshore-container manufacturing, structural modifications, interior fit-outs, electrical and HVAC installations, prototype testing, and certification support. This qualifies the company as the container-fabrication layer of a modular mission solution, but the reviewed public candidate must not assert the private PA-4 relationship or a defence-customer relationship without public corroboration.

source.title: Weatherhaven Mobile Expandable Container Configuration
source.locator: MECC product overview, applications, transport, deployment, and outfitting sections
source.summary: Weatherhaven describes a self-contained expandable shelter with an ISO shipping footprint, ISO and CSC transport certification, electrical, mechanical and HVAC fit-outs, and configurations for command, medical, maintenance, laboratory, and hazardous-material roles.

leads.evidenceLocator: Official MECC, military workshop, company history, and Government of Canada HQSS pages
followUpQuestions: Which MECC or TRECC variants are currently offered for naval or shipborne use?
Which approved product imagery may be shown on the public dossier?
leads.roleSpecificEvidence: The official product page establishes a fully outfitted ISO-container-based shelter that expands to three times its packed floor area and supports command, medical, workshop, laboratory, and emergency roles. The company and Canadian government pages corroborate long-standing military work and Weatherhaven's Headquarters Shelter System award.

source.title: DEW Military-Grade Integrated Shelters
source.locator: Shelters product overview and Medium Support Vehicle System sections
source.summary: DEW describes military-grade rigid and expandable shelters outfitted as command posts, clinics, kitchens, and workshops, including 28 Medium Support Vehicle System variants and configurations transported by land, sea, or air.

leads.evidenceLocator: Official shelter product, CBRN case study, facilities, contact, and DND mobile-workspace pages
followUpQuestions: Which current shelter variants are available for maritime deployment or naval integration?
Should the Miramichi production facility be added as a secondary published location?
leads.roleSpecificEvidence: DEW's official product and case-study pages establish the company as an integrator that turns rigid, expandable, and ISO containers into command, medical, maintenance, and CBRN systems. A DND release corroborates 994 baseline container shelters and 846 functional kits delivered for Canadian Armed Forces mobile workspaces.

source.title: VARD 7 115 Next Generation Offshore Patrol Vessel
source.locator: Approval in Principle announcement and mission-bay description
source.summary: Vard Marine states that its ABS-approved offshore patrol vessel design includes a multi-mission bay and set-down area for containerized mission payloads supporting air, surface, and sub-surface missions.

leads.evidenceLocator: Official VARD 7 115, VARD 7 078, Vigilance, corporate, and public contact pages
followUpQuestions: Which container interfaces are part of a delivered vessel rather than a concept or approval-in-principle design?
Which modular payload integrations are performed directly by Vard Marine versus Team Vigilance partners?
leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Vard Marine's official design pages show how standard ISO containers and containerized payloads can be planned into a naval platform: the VARD 7 078 flex bay holds up to four ISO containers, the VARD 7 115 includes a multi-mission bay and payload set-down area, and Vigilance integrates a plug-and-play mission-module handling system.

source.title: Navamar Sea-to-Shore Connector System
source.locator: Sea-to-Shore Connector project and factory acceptance test sections
source.summary: Navamar describes four modular Sea-to-Shore Connector systems built for the Royal Canadian Navy's Joint Support Ships, including modular pontoons, a 50-tonne payload, roll-on and roll-off access, and transport of vehicles or sea containers.

leads.evidenceLocator: Official Navamar project page plus PSPC and Royal Canadian Navy project corroboration
followUpQuestions: Have all four Sea-to-Shore Connector systems been delivered and accepted?
What current modular vessel or containerized logistics projects may be described publicly?
leads.roleSpecificEvidence: Navamar's page, a Public Services and Procurement Canada feature, and a Royal Canadian Navy article establish a delivered Canadian modular naval project. The system packs into container-like modules, assembles in sheltered water, carries vehicles or sea containers, and can be reconfigured for logistics, bridge, dock, diving, maintenance, and disaster-response work.
